prompt: Some people believe that university education should be free for all students. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
promptCn: 有人认为大学教育应该对所有学生免费。你在多大程度上同意或不同意？
ideas: 免学费能扩大入学机会
全部免费会给财政带来压力、降低教学质量
更好的做法是适度收费 + 定向资助
outline: Intro: 改写题目并表明部分不同意
Body 1: 免费教育的好处——人才不因贫困流失
Body 2: 全部免费的问题——财政压力与公平性
Conclusion: 支持定向资助而非全面免费
phrases: While I accept that ..., I believe ...
The strongest argument for ... is that ...
A more balanced approach would be to ...
modelAnswer:
In many countries, the cost of a degree has risen sharply, and this has led some people to argue that higher education should be paid for entirely by the state. While I accept that free tuition would widen access, I believe a fully free system is neither fair nor sustainable, and that targeted support is a better solution.

The strongest argument for free university education is that talent is spread evenly across society, but money is not. When fees are high, capable students from low-income families may decide not to apply at all, and the country loses doctors, engineers and teachers it badly needs. Removing fees would send a clear message that higher education is open to everyone, regardless of family background.

However, making every course free for every student has serious drawbacks. Universities are expensive to run, and if the full cost falls on taxpayers, governments are likely to cap the number of places or reduce spending per student. In practice, this can mean larger classes, older equipment and fewer support services. It is also questionable whether a factory worker should pay, through taxes, for the degree of someone who will later earn twice as much.

A more balanced approach would be to charge moderate fees while offering generous grants to students from poorer backgrounds and allowing graduates to repay loans only when their income reaches a certain level. This protects access for those who need help most without placing an unlimited burden on public finances.

In conclusion, although free tuition appears attractive, I disagree that it should be extended to all students. Financial help should be directed at those who need it most, so that universities remain both open and well funded.

prompt: The bar chart below shows the percentage of households with internet access in three countries in 2000, 2010 and 2020. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
keyFeatures: 三国上网家庭比例 20 年间都大幅上升
A 国始终最高，C 国最低但第二个十年增速最快
modelAnswer:
The bar chart compares the proportion of households that had internet access in three countries in 2000, 2010 and 2020.

Overall, internet access rose considerably in all three countries over the twenty-year period. Country A had the highest rate throughout, while Country C remained the lowest, although it showed the most rapid growth in the second decade.

In 2000, just over a third of households in Country A were connected, compared with 20% in Country B and only 8% in Country C. Over the following ten years, the figure for Country A roughly doubled to 72%, and Country B saw a similar increase to 55%. Country C also improved, reaching 30%.

By 2020, access in Country A had become almost universal at 95%, with Country B not far behind at 88%. Country C more than doubled its 2010 figure to 64%, but it still lagged well behind the other two countries.

In short, the gap between the three countries narrowed over time, but clear differences in access remained at the end of the period.

prompt: You recently stayed at a friend's flat while they were away. Write a letter to your friend. In your letter: thank them for letting you stay; describe a problem that happened during your stay; explain what you have done about it.
bullets: thank them for letting you stay
describe a problem that happened during your stay
explain what you have done about it
modelAnswer:
Dear Anna,

Thank you so much for letting me stay at your flat last week. It was the perfect base for my training course, and it was lovely to come back each evening to such a quiet and comfortable place. Your neighbour, Mr Davies, was also very kind and showed me how the heating worked on my first night.

Unfortunately, I have to tell you about a small accident. On Thursday morning, while I was watering your plants, I knocked the large blue vase off the windowsill and it broke into several pieces. Luckily, no water reached the carpet, but I felt terrible about it.

I have already ordered the same vase from the shop where you bought it, and it should be delivered to your flat on Monday. Mr Davies has kindly agreed to take it in for you. If it does not arrive, please let me know and I will sort it out straight away.

Thanks again for your generosity. I hope I can return the favour when you next visit my city.

Best wishes,
Lucy
